title: RigSpec
description: A guitar or bass signal chain described independently of any device file format. Every input path — a text description, an artist name, a recording, a captured amp — resolves to a RigSpec, and everything that writes a device preset consumes one. RigSpec is not a Line 6 concept; it is this project's own intermediate representation.

name.description: Human-readable name for the rig. Becomes the preset name.

blocks.description: The chain, in no particular array order. Placement is carried by each block's dsp and pos, not by array index.

snapshots.description: Named parameter variations over the same chain.

origin.description: How this rig was decided. Distinct from a catalog entry's provenance, which records how the catalog learned about a block. A rig has one origin; the blocks it references each carry their own provenance.

modelId.description: A device-internal model identifier, such as HD2_AmpAmpegSVT. Opaque to this schema — validity is decided against a catalog, not here.

paramValue.description: One parameter value. Device parameters mix floats, integers, booleans and enumerated strings within a single object, so the JSON type carries the kind. A number literal without a decimal point or exponent is an integer; any other number is a float.

params.description: Parameter values keyed by the device's own parameter key, such as Gain or Mode.

dsp.description: Which DSP processor this block occupies. Zero-based.

pos.description: Position within its processor. Positions on one processor must form the contiguous run 0..n-1.

enabled.description: Whether the block is active. A disabled block still occupies its processor and still costs DSP.

overrides.description: Parameter overrides keyed by the index of the block in the blocks array. JSON object keys are strings, so an index appears as "0", not 0.
